body: The European Union Aviation Safety Agency (EASA) has ordered operators of ATR 42 and ATR 72 turboprops to check their de-icing systems as often as every 160 flight hours, warning that a valve failure could go undetected until an aircraft encounters icing and lead to an unrecoverable loss of control. The airworthiness directive, issued November 16, 2026, takes effect November 30.

EASA had already shortened the time between checks in January 2025 after a design review identified the risk. A subsequent analysis of how the valves could fail prompted ATR to revise its maintenance instructions again in October. Brazilian investigators identified ice buildup and multiple de-icing system failures among the factors that contributed to the August 9, 2024, crash of Voepass Flight 2283. All 62 people aboard the ATR 72-500 died when it crashed in Vinhedo, Brazil. ATR issued its first notice to operators about the valve checks in October 2024, about two months after the accident.

The order covers the valves that regulate pressure and shut off the air supply to the de-icing system. How often operators must test them depends on the aircraft model and whether ATR modified it at the factory or an operator had the work done later. The biggest change is for modified ATR 42-400s, ATR 42-500s and ATR 72s. Under the January 2025 order, those aircraft could fly up to 1,050 hours between checks. The new limit is 160 hours, an 85% reduction. For aircraft of the same models without the modification, the interval drops from 700 hours to 210. Operators of the earlier ATR 42-200, -300 and -320 models will have to check the valves every 190 hours, down from 650. If a valve fails a check, the operator must correct the problem before the aircraft flies again. If ATR's published instructions do not cover the fault, the operator must obtain approved instructions from the manufacturer and carry out the work.
en.summary: The European Union Aviation Safety Agency has ordered operators of ATR 42 and ATR 72 turboprops to inspect their de-icing system valves as often as every 160 flight hours, warning that an undetected valve failure could lead to an unrecoverable loss of control in icing.
en.title: EASA orders more frequent ATR de-icing system checks over loss-of-control risk

body: 歐洲航空安全總署（EASA）已下令ATR 42與ATR 72渦輪螺旋槳飛機的營運商，每160飛行小時檢查一次除冰系統，以防閥門故障在飛機遭遇結冰前未被發現，進而導致無法挽回的失控。這項適航指令於2026年11月16日發布、11月30日生效。
EASA曾在2025年1月設計審查發現風險後縮短檢查間隔；後續針對閥門失效模式的分析促使ATR於10月再度修訂維修指示。巴西調查人員認定，結冰與多重除冰系統失效是2024年8月9日沃帕斯航空2283號班機墜毀的肇因之一，該架ATR 72-500在巴西維涅杜墜毀，機上62人全數罹難；ATR於事故約兩個月後的2024年10月首度向營運商發布閥門檢查通告。

這項指令涵蓋調節壓力並切斷除冰系統供氣的閥門，檢查頻率依機型與是否經原廠改裝而定。改裝後的ATR 42-400、ATR 42-500與ATR 72檢查間隔由1,050小時縮短至160小時，減幅達85%；同型未改裝飛機由700小時降至210小時；較早期的ATR 42-200、-300與-320則由650小時降至190小時。閥門未通過檢查時，營運商須在飛機再次飛行前排除故障；若ATR公布的指示未涵蓋該故障，營運商須向製造商取得核准指示並依指示施工。
zh.summary: 歐洲航空安全總署發布適航指令，要求ATR 42與ATR 72機隊更頻繁檢查除冰系統閥門，最短每160飛行小時檢查一次，以防閥門故障在結冰時未被發現而導致無法挽回的失控。
zh.title: EASA下令ATR 42／72飛機縮短除冰系統檢查間隔 防範失控風險
